title: Perfect local models, smooth duals and trace contractions under finite reduction
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq m\geq1$. Put $A_i=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^i)$ for $i=n,m$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, set $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and assume $a_X:X\to s$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible at both stages. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories, normalized smooth orientation, Tate twists, duals and cohomology of [def-pod-conventions]. Write $F_T=-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$ for derived change of coefficient rings on $T=X,s$, with target the $A_m$-category [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ be site-perfect [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] and put $K_m=F_XK_n$. On every cover with a bounded finite-projective model $P^\bullet$ for $K_n$, the termwise model $P^\bullet\otimes_{A_n}A_m$ represents $K_m$ and is bounded finite-projective. More explicitly, finite-free splittings $P^j\xrightarrow{i_j}A_{n,U}^{N_j}\xrightarrow{p_j}P^j$, $p_ji_j=1$, induce splittings of the reduced terms through $A_{m,U}^{N_j}$ with the same ranks and degree bounds. Both models are K-flat. The object $K_m$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_m)$ and is site-perfect, and both $K_i$ are perfect over $A_{i,X}$ in [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x].

Put $K_i^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{A_i}(K_i,A_{i,X})$, $L_i=K_i^\vee(d)[2d]$, and let $e_i:K_i\otimes^L_{A_i}L_i\to A_{i,X}(d)[2d]$ be the shifted twisted evaluation [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x]. The complexes $L_i$ are site-perfect objects of $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_i)$. The canonical internal-Hom and twist comparisons give isomorphisms
$$v:F_X(K_n^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_m^\vee,\qquad \lambda:F_XL_n\xrightarrow{\sim}L_m,$$
carrying $F_X(e_n)$ to $e_m$ under the tensor and orientation-unit comparisons. The orientation-induced identifications $\mathbb D_XK_i\cong L_i$ commute with these comparisons and with evaluation.

Write $c_M:F_sR\Gamma_c(X,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,F_XM)$ for the canonical compact-support comparison, natural in $M$. Let $t_i:R\Gamma_c(X,A_{i,X}(d)[2d])\to A_i$ be the normalized smooth trace [def-pur-smooth-trace], and define $\tau_i=t_i\circ R\Gamma_c(X,e_i)$. Under $\lambda$, the tensor comparisons and $F_sA_n\cong A_m$, one has
$$F_s(t_n)=t_m\circ c_{A_{n,X}(d)[2d]},\qquad F_s(\tau_n)=\tau_m\circ c_{K_n\otimes^L L_n}.$$
All displayed equalities and isomorphisms are in the derived categories; no flatness of $A_m$ over $A_n$ is assumed.

source.place: First paragraph: site-perfect internal-Hom and evaluation comparisons, normalized trace and smooth orientation; returned proof steps 1-2 and the evaluation/trace part of step 4.

proof.text: Work on any covering member $U$ carrying the stated model $P^\bullet$. Each term is a retract of $A_{n,U}^{N_j}$. Tensoring a short exact sequence with that term gives a retract of the $N_j$-fold direct sum of the sequence, hence remains exact; thus the terms are flat. The bounded-above flat-complex theorem makes $P^\bullet$ K-flat. Tensor the splitting maps with $A_{m,U}$: $(p_j\otimes1)(i_j\otimes1)=(p_ji_j)\otimes1=1$, and $A_{n,U}^{N_j}\otimes_{A_n}A_m=A_{m,U}^{N_j}$. The reduced terms are therefore finite projective with the same finite-free ambient ranks, and zero degrees stay zero. The same retract argument makes them flat, and the same K-flat theorem applies to their bounded complex. K-flat computation of derived change of rings now gives $F_U(K_n|_U)\cong P^\bullet\otimes_{A_n}A_m$. The canonical pullback-composition comparison for the identity-topos coefficient map and restriction to $U$ identifies this with $(F_XK_n)|_U$. Consequently these are local finite-projective models for $K_m$; no projectivity in the global abelian category of sheaves is claimed.

proof.text: The finite-reduction functor in [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] is explicitly typed $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)\to D^b_{ctf}(T,A_m)$ for separated finite-type $k$-schemes $T$. Apply its domain assertion at $T=X$ to $K_n$ to obtain $K_m\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_m)$. Together with the local models of step 1 this proves site-perfectness at both stages. The finite-level definitions of site-perfectness and perfectness over $A_{i,X}$ agree, so both $K_i$ satisfy the latter condition. Here $X$ and $s$ satisfy the scheme hypotheses, $1\le m\le n$, and $\ell$ is invertible because $\ell\ne p$.

source.place: First paragraph: coefficient dual, evaluation and normalized smooth trace

proof.text: For $i=n,m$, apply [lem-pod-coefficient-dual-perfect] to $K_i$: the coefficient dual $K_i^\vee$ is perfect and belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_i)$. The finite-level twist theorem says $A_{i,X}(d)$ is a locally constant invertible rank-one module and twisting preserves $D^b_{ctf}$. On a common refinement trivializing this line and a finite-projective model for $K_i^\vee$, tensoring with the line leaves a bounded finite-projective model; shifting by $[2d]$ just reindexes it. Shifts preserve bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude by translating the vanishing interval in their definition. Hence $L_i=K_i^\vee(d)[2d]$ is site-perfect and lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_i)$.

source.place: First paragraph: coefficient dual, evaluation and normalized smooth trace

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-site-perfect-scalar-hom] with $R=A_{n,X}$, $S=A_{m,X}$, $P=K_n$ and $Q=A_{n,X}$. Its natural isomorphism, followed by the coefficient-unit identification, is exactly $v:F_X(K_n^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_m^\vee$. Its statement defines this arrow as the transpose of reduced evaluation, so the evaluation square commutes for this specified arrow. Compose $v(d)[2d]$ with the canonical twist-and-shift reduction isomorphism of [lem-pur-finite-tensor-presentation-reduction]; this is $\lambda:F_XL_n\xrightarrow{\sim}L_m$. That theorem identifies the twist reassociators and shift comparisons, and [lem-fix-operation-reduction] preserves tensor associators and evaluations. Tensoring the evaluation square with the line and applying its shift therefore gives, with $U_i=A_{i,X}(d)[2d]$, the equation $h\circ F_X(e_n)=e_m\circ b$, where $h:F_XU_n\xrightarrow{\sim}(F_XA_{n,X})(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}U_m$ is the twist-and-shift reduction isomorphism of [lem-pur-finite-tensor-presentation-reduction] at $L=A_{n,X}$ followed by the coefficient-unit identification $F_XA_{n,X}\cong A_{m,X}$ (the same comparisons [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons] used by the vertical maps of [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]), and $b:F_X(K_n\otimes^LL_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_m\otimes^LL_m$ uses $\lambda$ and the canonical tensor map.

source.place: First paragraph: coefficient dual, evaluation and normalized smooth trace

proof.text: Apply [thm-sf-dual-perfect] at each finite coefficient stage to the perfect $K_i$. It supplies the orientation-induced isomorphism $\mathbb D_XK_i\cong K_i^\vee(d)[2d]=L_i$, and its stated compatibility with finite reduction and the canonical evaluation gives precisely the square with $v$ and $\lambda$ of step 4. The normalized orientation is the one fixed in the hypotheses; the finite-reduction purity theorem identifies its reductions with that same normalized orientation at level $m$. Thus no choice of an unrelated duality isomorphism is being substituted.

source.place: First paragraph: coefficient dual, evaluation and normalized smooth trace

proof.text: Specialize the compact-support comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] to $a_X:X\to s$. It gives the canonical natural isomorphism $c_M:F_sR\Gamma_c(X,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,F_XM)$ on the finite-Tor domain. The trace is the exceptional counit after the smooth orientation, as specified by [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Apply the smooth-trace compatibility clause of [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] to $f=a_X$ and the point coefficient unit. Its vertical twist-and-unit identification on $F_XU_n$ is the $h$ of step 4, since both are built from the finite-reduction comparisons of [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons] in the chart normalization fixed by [lem-pur-finite-tensor-presentation-reduction]. Hence its equation is $F_s(t_n)=t_m\circ R\Gamma_c(X,h)\circ c_{U_n}$, which is the first displayed identity of the item under the orientation-unit identification. The admissibility required for the coefficient comparisons of exceptional adjoints is assumed at both stages, and $a_X$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$.

source.place: First paragraph: coefficient dual, evaluation and normalized smooth trace

proof.text:
Put $B_i=K_i\otimes^LL_i$. These objects are in $D^b_{ctf}$ by the tensor-preservation theorem, so the comparison may be applied to $e_n:B_n\to U_n$. Naturality gives
$$c_{U_n}\circ F_sR\Gamma_c(e_n)=R\Gamma_c(F_Xe_n)\circ c_{B_n}.$$
Use functoriality, the trace equation of step 6, and the evaluation equation $h\circ F_X(e_n)=e_m\circ b$ of step 4 to compute
$$\begin{aligned}
F_s(\tau_n)&=F_s(t_n)\circ F_sR\Gamma_c(e_n)\\
&=t_m\circ R\Gamma_c(h)\circ R\Gamma_c(F_Xe_n)\circ c_{B_n}\\
&=t_m\circ R\Gamma_c(e_m)\circ R\Gamma_c(b)\circ c_{B_n}\\
&=\tau_m\circ R\Gamma_c(b)\circ c_{B_n}.
\end{aligned}$$
Under $b$ and $F_sA_n\cong A_m$ this is exactly the second displayed identity. Every functor and comparison used here is derived; the retract and K-flat arguments in step 1 never use flatness of $A_m$ as an $A_n$-module.
